summary: Specifies an EDNS option so secondary DNS servers can honor the SOA EXPIRE field as if transferring from the primary, even through other secondaries. It is experimental.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 7314 adds an EDNS option that carries a DNS zone's expiry information between servers. This lets secondary servers preserve the expiry behavior even when they transfer from another secondary.

questions: how does dns zone expiry work
what is the edns expire option
how does soa expire work through secondaries
subtitle: An EDNS option to preserve DNS zone expiry through secondary servers.

tldr.problem: A secondary DNS server's SOA EXPIRE behavior can be extended unintentionally when zone transfers pass through other secondaries.
tldr.mechanism: The EDNS EXPIRE option carries the current expiry value in a query response so a secondary can maintain the zone's expiry behavior across transfer paths.
tldr.outcome: RFC 7314 describes an Experimental mechanism intended to stop stale zone content from being served indefinitely.

today: RFC 7314 is Experimental. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Expiry Through Transfer Chains
sections.content: The SOA EXPIRE field indicates when a secondary should discard zone contents after it cannot contact the primary. The RFC explains that secondary servers may transfer from other secondaries for robustness or reachability. Without extra information, transfer delays or loops can make the effective expiry period longer than intended.
sections.plainLanguage: A secondary should stop serving a zone after its expiry timer runs out. If it copies from another secondary, it needs information that prevents the deadline from being extended by the copy.

sections.title: The EDNS EXPIRE Option
sections.content: A query may include a zero-length EDNS EXPIRE option, usually for SOA, AXFR, or IXFR queries involved in zone maintenance. A primary returns the SOA EXPIRE value; a secondary returns its current expiry timer. The response value is four bytes and is expressed in seconds in network byte order.
sections.plainLanguage: A secondary adds the option to a zone refresh or transfer query. The server replies with its expiry value so the secondary can update its timer.

sections.title: Secondary Server Behavior
sections.content: A secondary includes the option in zone-transfer requests and refresh queries. When it receives the option in an SOA response or an up-to-date IXFR response, it updates its timer using the maximum of the returned value and its current timer. After an AXFR or IXFR transfer, it should use the returned option value to initialize the timer, subject to the SOA EXPIRE field rule in the RFC.
sections.plainLanguage: The secondary uses expiry information from the response when setting its timer. The RFC also says the SOA EXPIRE value must be used as a maximum in the stated cases.
